investigation.title: Remote Agent Pod Unschedulable: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 3 Remote-Agent Checks
investigation.summary: All three remote-agent checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed at 2026-07-15T06:57–07:05Z with an identical Kubernetes scheduling error: the 6-node production cluster has only 2 nodes carrying the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource, both of which are already at capacity, and the remaining 4 nodes do not satisfy the pod's node affinity/selector. Because the agent pod never scheduled, the eval runner never received a VM ID or a remote state value, leaving all four required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) absent and causing the expected-output contract to fail completely.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the production remote-agent swarm has exhausted its allocatable kata.peerpods.io/vm resource on the 2 eligible nodes. Every new remote-agent pod is rejected as Unschedulable before it can start, so no VM is provisioned, no agent identity is returned, and the eval runner cannot collect any of the four required evidence fields defined in the remote-agent-create contract (infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json line 256). This is an infrastructure capacity constraint, not an eval runner or contract configuration defect. No user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence, so impact is scoped to this observability eval at this time.

source-context.infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json:250-258: contract requires vmIdPresent=true and remoteState oneOf ['running','idle','ready'] — neither assertion can be evaluated when the pod never schedules.
possibleCauses: PRIMARY — kata.peerpods.io/vm resource exhaustion on the 2 eligible nodes: existing remote-agent pods are consuming all available VM slots, leaving zero capacity for new probe pods. This is directly stated in the scheduler message (evidence id: failed-check.message).

SECONDARY — node affinity/selector mismatch on the remaining 4 nodes: those nodes are not labeled or tainted to accept remote-agent pods, so even if VM capacity were freed, only 2 nodes are eligible. A misconfiguration or unintended label change on those 4 nodes could have reduced the schedulable pool.

TERTIARY — leaked or zombie remote-agent pods from prior eval runs holding VM slots: if cleanup (withCleanup in run-status-probes.mjs line 1883) failed on a previous run, stale pods may be occupying the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource without being active.

QUATERNARY — cluster under-provisioning: the 2 kata.peerpods.io/vm-capable nodes may have an insufficient VM quota for the concurrent load of multiple probe runs (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime all ran within the same ~8-minute window).

whatWouldDisproveThis: If the scheduler message were absent and the pod did schedule but the agent API returned an error, the root cause would be an application-layer failure rather than a capacity constraint.
If only remote-agent-create failed while remote-agent-state and remote-agent-runtime passed, the issue would be isolated to the create path rather than a shared infrastructure capacity problem.

If kubectl describe on the 2 eligible nodes showed available kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity at the time of the failure, the root cause would shift to a node affinity/selector misconfiguration rather than resource exhaustion.
If the eval runner's withCleanup function logged a successful cleanup of all prior probe pods, the zombie-pod hypothesis would be disproved.

If a re-run of the probe immediately after this failure succeeded without any cluster changes, the failure would be transient (e.g., a brief capacity spike) rather than a sustained exhaustion condition.
followUpEvals: Add a dedicated eval check that probes kata.peerpods.io/vm allocatable vs. allocated capacity on the eligible nodes and warns when headroom falls below a safe threshold (e.g., fewer than 1 free slot).
Add a zombie-pod detection eval that lists remote-agent pods older than a configurable TTL and fails if any are found, catching cleanup failures before they exhaust VM capacity.
Add a node-affinity coverage eval that verifies the number of nodes matching the remote-agent pod selector is above a minimum threshold, catching pool-shrinkage regressions early.

Consider splitting the remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, and remote-agent-runtime checks into staggered eval windows or adding a serialization gate so they do not compete for the same limited VM slots during a single observability run.

investigation.title: Remote Agents: All Three Checks Failing Due to Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity on Kubernetes Cluster
investigation.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed at 2026-07-15T07:00–07:05Z with an identical Kubernetes scheduler message: the cluster's 6 nodes cannot schedule new kata peer-pod VMs because 2 nodes report Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity and the remaining 4 nodes do not match the pod's node affinity/selector. Because the agent pod never scheduled, the eval runner's createAgent call in run-status-probes.mjs never returned an agent, and the expected-output contract for remote-agent-state received zero evidence (orgId, agentId, readyState, state all missing).
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the production-api remote-agents feature has exhausted its allocatable kata.peerpods.io/vm resource slots across the 2 nodes that carry that resource label. No preemption victims were available, and the 4 remaining nodes do not satisfy the pod's node affinity/selector. As a result, every eval attempt to provision a remote agent pod timed out unscheduled (~144–145 s), preventing the runner from reaching the state-polling step and producing any evidence. This is a Kubernetes infrastructure capacity constraint, not an application code defect. No user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence, so impact is scoped to the observability eval.

possibleCauses: PRIMARY — kata.peerpods.io/vm resource exhaustion on the 2 eligible nodes: all available VM slots are occupied by existing peer-pod workloads, leaving no capacity for the eval's new agent pod. Supported directly by failed-check.message and both sibling check messages.

SECONDARY — Node affinity/selector mismatch on 4 of 6 nodes: the remote-agent pod spec requires a node label or taint that only 2 nodes carry, and those 2 are already at capacity. This compounds the capacity issue and means horizontal scaling to other nodes is not possible without label/taint changes.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Pod Unschedulable: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 3 Remote-Agent Checks
investigations.summary: All three remote-agent checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed at 2026-07-15T06:57–07:05Z with an identical Kubernetes scheduling error: the 6-node production cluster has only 2 nodes carrying the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource, both of which are already at capacity, and the remaining 4 nodes do not satisfy the pod's node affinity/selector. Because the agent pod never scheduled, the eval runner never received a VM ID or a remote state value, leaving all four required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) absent and causing the expected-output contract to fail completely.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the production remote-agent swarm has exhausted its allocatable kata.peerpods.io/vm resource on the 2 eligible nodes. Every new remote-agent pod is rejected as Unschedulable before it can start, so no VM is provisioned, no agent identity is returned, and the eval runner cannot collect any of the four required evidence fields defined in the remote-agent-create contract (infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json line 256). This is an infrastructure capacity constraint, not an eval runner or contract configuration defect. No user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence, so impact is scoped to this observability eval at this time.

source-context.infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json:250-258: contract requires vmIdPresent=true and remoteState oneOf ['running','idle','ready'] — neither assertion can be evaluated when the pod never schedules.
possibleCauses: PRIMARY — kata.peerpods.io/vm resource exhaustion on the 2 eligible nodes: existing remote-agent pods are consuming all available VM slots, leaving zero capacity for new probe pods. This is directly stated in the scheduler message (evidence id: failed-check.message).

SECONDARY — node affinity/selector mismatch on the remaining 4 nodes: those nodes are not labeled or tainted to accept remote-agent pods, so even if VM capacity were freed, only 2 nodes are eligible. A misconfiguration or unintended label change on those 4 nodes could have reduced the schedulable pool.

TERTIARY — leaked or zombie remote-agent pods from prior eval runs holding VM slots: if cleanup (withCleanup in run-status-probes.mjs line 1883) failed on a previous run, stale pods may be occupying the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource without being active.

QUATERNARY — cluster under-provisioning: the 2 kata.peerpods.io/vm-capable nodes may have an insufficient VM quota for the concurrent load of multiple probe runs (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime all ran within the same ~8-minute window).

whatWouldDisproveThis: If the scheduler message were absent and the pod did schedule but the agent API returned an error, the root cause would be an application-layer failure rather than a capacity constraint.
If only remote-agent-create failed while remote-agent-state and remote-agent-runtime passed, the issue would be isolated to the create path rather than a shared infrastructure capacity problem.

If a re-run of the probe immediately after this failure succeeded without any cluster changes, the failure would be transient (e.g., a brief capacity spike) rather than a sustained exhaustion condition.
followUpEvals: Add a dedicated eval check that probes kata.peerpods.io/vm allocatable vs. allocated capacity on the eligible nodes and warns when headroom falls below a safe threshold (e.g., fewer than 1 free slot).
Add a zombie-pod detection eval that lists remote-agent pods older than a configurable TTL and fails if any are found, catching cleanup failures before they exhaust VM capacity.
Add a node-affinity coverage eval that verifies the number of nodes matching the remote-agent pod selector is above a minimum threshold, catching pool-shrinkage regressions early.

Consider splitting the remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, and remote-agent-runtime checks into staggered eval windows or adding a serialization gate so they do not compete for the same limited VM slots during a single observability run.

This is a Kubernetes infrastructure capacity constraint, not an application code defect. investigations.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Nodes
investigations.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api at 2026-07-15T07:02–07:05Z because the Kubernetes scheduler could not place the remote agent pod: 2 of 6 nodes reported Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. Because the pod never became schedulable, the agent was never created, and the eval produced zero evidence — all 5 required contract fields (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message) are missing.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the production-api remote-agents feature has exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm resource quota on the two nodes that are eligible by affinity/selector. The scheduler message "0/6 nodes are available: 2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector" and "No preemption victims found" confirms that no schedulable capacity exists and preemption cannot recover it. The pod remained unscheduled for ~145 seconds until the eval timed out, preventing any agent lifecycle progress and leaving the expected-output contract entirely unmet. This is an eval-observed infrastructure capacity failure; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.
proof: failed-check.message: scheduler reports '0/6 nodes are available: 2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector. preemption: 0/6 nodes are available: 2 No preemption victims found for incoming pod, 4 Preemption is not helpful for scheduling.'
failed-check.timing: latencyMs=149944, pod stuck unscheduled for 145s before eval timeout at endedAt=2026-07-15T07:05:07.651Z
failed-check.evidence: evidence object is empty — zero fields returned, confirming the agent was never created or reached
expected-output.missing-required-evidence: all 5 contract fields missing — orgId, agentId, model, provider, message — because pod scheduling never completed
sibling.remote-agent-create: same Unschedulable message, latencyMs=149979, endedAt=2026-07-15T07:00:07.631Z — the create step failed first with identical scheduler output
sibling.remote-agent-state: same Unschedulable message, latencyMs=150076, endedAt=2026-07-15T07:02:37.707Z — state polling also failed because no agent was ever running

source-context.infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs:1910-1918: runner calls createAgent(args, track, 'remote', null, orgId) at line 1918, which is the step that triggers pod scheduling and would block indefinitely if the pod cannot be placed

source-context.infra/evals/status/features.json:181-189: remote-agent-runtime is registered as required=false with outageLatencyMs=420000; the eval failed at ~150s, well within the outage threshold, confirming the failure is a hard scheduling block not a latency regression
possibleCauses: Primary — kata.peerpods.io/vm resource exhaustion on the 2 affinity-eligible nodes: the cluster has consumed all available peer-pod VM slots on the only nodes that match the remote agent pod's node affinity/selector, leaving no schedulable capacity and no preemption candidates.

Secondary — node affinity/selector misconfiguration or drift: 4 of 6 nodes do not match the pod's affinity/selector at all, meaning the schedulable pool is already constrained to 2 nodes. If affinity rules were recently tightened or node labels changed, the effective capacity could have dropped without any change to the VM quota itself.

Tertiary — cluster under-provisioning for concurrent eval runs: all three sibling checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) ran sequentially within a ~5-minute window and each consumed or contended for the same kata.peerpods.io/vm slots, potentially exhausting capacity across back-to-back runs.

Lower confidence — transient VM slot leak or slow release: a prior agent pod may not have released its kata.peerpods.io/vm allocation before the eval run started, temporarily reducing available capacity below the required minimum.

reproductionSteps.label: Run only the remote-agent-runtime eval probe against production-api
reproductionSteps.details: Use the same environment variables as the scheduled observability workflow. Observe whether the pod scheduling failure message recurs.

reproductionSteps.label: Run all three remote-agents sibling checks together to confirm shared scheduling bottleneck
reproductionSteps.details: If all three fail with the same Unschedulable message, the root cause is cluster-level capacity, not a per-check issue.

reproductionSteps.label: Inspect current kata.peerpods.io/vm allocatable and used capacity on the 2 affinity-eligible nodes
reproductionSteps.details: Use cluster tooling (e.g., kubectl describe node) to check the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource field on each node that matches the remote agent pod's affinity/selector. Compare allocatable vs. requested to confirm exhaustion.

reproductionSteps.label: List currently running or pending remote agent pods to identify leaked or stuck allocations
reproductionSteps.details: Check for pods in Running, Pending, or Terminating state that hold kata.peerpods.io/vm slots and have not been released, which would explain why no capacity is available for new eval pods.

reproductionSteps.label: Verify node labels and affinity rules to confirm 4 nodes are intentionally excluded
reproductionSteps.details: Inspect the node affinity/selector on the remote agent pod spec and compare against node labels on all 6 nodes to determine whether the 4 non-matching nodes are excluded by design or by a label drift.

affectedAreas.label: Remote Agents — Kubernetes pod scheduling layer (kata.peerpods.io/vm resource)
affectedAreas.reason: The scheduler explicitly reports Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm on the 2 nodes eligible by affinity, blocking all remote agent pod creation. This is the earliest violated boundary in the eval execution path (evidenced by failed-check.message and sibling.remote-agent-create).

affectedAreas.label: Remote Agents — Node affinity/selector pool
affectedAreas.reason: 4 of 6 cluster nodes do not match the remote agent pod's node affinity/selector (failed-check.message), constraining the schedulable pool to only 2 nodes and amplifying the impact of any VM slot exhaustion on those nodes.

affectedAreas.label: Remote Agents feature — all three eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime)
affectedAreas.reason: All three checks under the remote-agents feature (lines 183–185) failed with the same underlying scheduler error, confirming the entire remote agent provisioning path is blocked in production-api at the time of the eval run.

affectedAreas.label: Eval runner — createAgent call for remote agent type
affectedAreas.reason: The runner at line 1918 calls createAgent(args, track, 'remote', null, orgId), which triggers pod scheduling. This call never completes because the pod cannot be placed, causing the probe to time out and return empty evidence.

recommendedNextActions: Immediately check kata.peerpods.io/vm allocatable and used capacity on the 2 affinity-eligible nodes to confirm exhaustion and determine how many slots are consumed vs. available.
Identify and terminate any leaked, stuck, or zombie remote agent pods that are holding kata.peerpods.io/vm slots without active workloads, to restore scheduling capacity.

Verify that all 6 cluster nodes have the expected labels and that the remote agent pod's node affinity/selector is correctly configured; if 4 nodes are unintentionally excluded, restoring their labels would expand the schedulable pool.

Review whether the eval run schedule causes back-to-back remote agent pod creation (remote-agent-create → remote-agent-state → remote-agent-runtime) that exhausts the VM quota before prior pods are released, and consider staggering runs or increasing cleanup aggressiveness.

If VM slot capacity is genuinely exhausted by legitimate workloads, escalate to the infrastructure team to provision additional kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity on the eligible nodes or expand the affinity-eligible node pool.

Note that remote-agent-runtime is registered as required=false (infra/evals/status/features.json line 185), so this failure does not by itself constitute a declared outage, but the co-failure of required siblings remote-agent-create and remote-agent-state (required=true, lines 183–184) means the remote-agents feature is in a degraded or outage state per the degradedAfterFailures=1 / outageAfterFailures=2 thresholds.

recommendedVerifierProbes.label: Re-run remote-agent-runtime eval probe in isolation
recommendedVerifierProbes.reason: Confirms whether the scheduling failure is persistent or has self-resolved. A pass would indicate transient exhaustion; a repeat fail with the same message confirms sustained capacity exhaustion.

recommendedVerifierProbes.label: Re-run all three remote-agents sibling checks together
recommendedVerifierProbes.reason: Determines whether the failure is isolated to one check or affects the entire remote-agents provisioning path, which would confirm a shared infrastructure dependency failure.

recommendedVerifierProbes.label: Inspect kata.peerpods.io/vm resource capacity on affinity-eligible nodes
recommendedVerifierProbes.reason: Directly confirms or refutes the VM slot exhaustion hypothesis by showing allocatable vs. used capacity on the 2 nodes that match the pod's affinity/selector.

recommendedVerifierProbes.label: List all pods holding kata.peerpods.io/vm allocations in the cluster
recommendedVerifierProbes.reason: Identifies whether leaked, stuck, or long-running pods are consuming VM slots that should have been released, explaining why no capacity is available for new eval pods.

recommendedVerifierProbes.label: Inspect node labels on all 6 cluster nodes against the remote agent pod's affinity/selector
recommendedVerifierProbes.reason: Confirms whether the 4 non-matching nodes are excluded by design or by a label drift that has reduced the schedulable pool below its intended size.

whatWouldDisproveThis: If kubectl describe node on the 2 affinity-eligible nodes shows kata.peerpods.io/vm allocatable capacity available and no pods currently consuming it, the exhaustion hypothesis would be disproved and the cause would shift to a scheduler plugin bug or misconfigured resource request on the pod spec.

If a re-run of the eval immediately after this failure succeeds and produces all 5 required evidence fields, the failure was transient (e.g., a slow VM slot release) rather than a sustained capacity exhaustion.
If the 4 non-matching nodes are found to have the correct labels and the affinity rules are confirmed unchanged, the node affinity drift hypothesis would be disproved.
If no kata.peerpods.io/vm resource is defined on any node in the cluster, the failure would indicate a missing resource registration rather than exhaustion.

If the eval runner logs show the pod was never submitted to the scheduler (e.g., an API auth error before pod creation), the scheduler message would be a secondary artifact and the root cause would be upstream of scheduling.
followUpEvals: Add a pre-flight eval that checks kata.peerpods.io/vm allocatable vs. used capacity on affinity-eligible nodes before attempting remote agent creation, so scheduling exhaustion is surfaced as a distinct infrastructure capacity signal rather than a timeout.

Add an eval that counts the number of currently running or pending remote agent pods and alerts if it approaches the kata.peerpods.io/vm quota ceiling, providing early warning before eval runs are blocked.
Add a node-affinity coverage eval that verifies the expected number of nodes match the remote agent pod's affinity/selector, catching label drift before it reduces the schedulable pool.
Consider a post-cleanup eval that confirms kata.peerpods.io/vm slots are released within an expected window after each remote agent eval run, detecting slot leaks before they accumulate across runs.
